lines: TERM
MEANING

children.title: SIEM
lines: Security Information & Event Management - collect → normalize → detect → correlate → alert → retain.

children.title: Attribution
lines: Mapping an event to the workload/identity that caused it (container → session → project) - the layer that makes findings actionable.

children.title: eBPF
lines: Linux kernel technology to run sandboxed programs in the kernel - syscall/network observation and enforcement without app instrumentation.

children.title: LSM / BPF-LSM
lines: Linux Security Module hook framework (optionally via eBPF) - synchronous enforcement: deny syscalls before they execute.

children.title: XDP / XDP_DROP
lines: eXpress Data Path - eBPF programs attached at the NIC; XDP_DROP discards packets at the driver, before the TCP stack.

children.title: RCF
lines: Random Cut Forest - unsupervised streaming anomaly-detection algorithm (used by OpenSearch AD and AWS GuardDuty-class services).

children.title: FIM
lines: File Integrity Monitoring - watching sensitive files for unauthorized changes.

children.title: IaC
lines: Infrastructure as Code - Terraform, CloudFormation, Helm, Kustomize, compose files; scannable by Checkov et al.

children.title: SBOM
lines: Software Bill of Materials - a machine-readable inventory of an artifact's components; CycloneDX is the common format.

children.title: HITL
lines: Human-in-the-Loop - irreversible actions wait for an operator decision; automation proposes, humans dispose.

children.title: Shadow API
lines: An endpoint that exists in traffic but not in documented routes/OpenAPI - the classic gateway-bypass surface.

children.title: Data Drift
lines: Model signal decay when live traffic distribution changes vs. training data - triggers retrain, not retuning of rules.

children.title: MTTR (p75)
lines: Mean Time To Respond/Remediate, 75th percentile - the runtime KPI containment playbooks can halve.

children.title: Blast Radius
lines: How much damage a compromise of one asset can do - the ranking dimension CSPM tools sort findings by.

children.title: Warm-start model
lines: A globally trained baseline, fine-tuned per tenant - cheaper than per-tenant training and still isolated.

children.title: OCSF / ASFF
lines: Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework / AWS Security Finding Format - schemas that make cross-source correlation possible.

children.title: Sigma
lines: Open signature format for detection rules (YAML), consumable by OpenSearch Security Analytics and friends.

children.title: Token binding
lines: Binding an API token to a client trait (e.g., TLS fingerprint) so a stolen token fails replay from another machine.
